Runs differ in how much protein was loaded and how well the instrument ran that day. Cyclic loess
removes those intensity-dependent differences so the 45 runs can be compared protein by protein.
Missing values stay missing: `03_Quantification` models them, and blood enters every later model as
a covariate.

## Packages

proteoDA supplies the normalisation and its standard reports. limma supplies the linear model used
for the variance check.

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(proteoDA)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(limma)
library(ggplot2)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "analysis_reporting_helpers.R"))
```

## Input

The input is the filtered `DAList` from `01_Protein_Filtering`: raw intensities with `NA` where a
protein was not detected.

```{r}
#| label: input
inputs <- c(filtered = "01_Processing/01_Protein_Filtering/c_data/DAList_filtered.rds")
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
dal <- readRDS(paths[["filtered"]])
out <- here("01_Processing", "02_Normalisation", "c_data")
reports <- here("01_Processing", "02_Normalisation", "b_reports")
for (path in c(out, reports)) dir.create(path, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

dim(dal$data)
dal$data[1:3, 1:4]
```

## Cyclic loess

Cyclic loess (Bolstad et al. 2003) takes every pair of runs, plots their log2 difference against
their mean intensity, fits a smooth curve through that cloud, and subtracts the curve. After a few
cycles no pair of runs differs systematically at any intensity. This is limma's
`normalizeCyclicLoess()`, called by proteoDA with `method = "fast"` (each run against the average
run) and limma's default adaptive span, so the curve's smoothness follows the protein count
(package behaviour). `normalize_data()` log2-transforms the raw intensities first; the `before`
matrix is logged here so the two can be compared on one scale.

proteoDA's reports go to `b_reports/`: `norm_comparison.pdf` scores every normalisation method it
offers, and `qc_pre.pdf` and `qc_post.pdf` show run-level QC before and after. The functions also
draw to the screen; a null device swallows that copy so it does not land in `Rplots.pdf`.

Choosing cyclic loess is a project decision. The manuscript's pipeline chose it independently,
after comparing eight methods on pooled coefficient of variation, median absolute deviation and
inter-run correlation. This repository holds no record of its own comparison beyond
`norm_comparison.pdf`.

```{r}
#| label: normalise
pdf(NULL)
write_norm_report(dal,
  grouping_column = "group", output_dir = reports,
  filename = "norm_comparison.pdf", overwrite = TRUE
)
write_qc_report(dal,
  color_column = "group", output_dir = reports,
  filename = "qc_pre.pdf", overwrite = TRUE
)
before <- log2(as.matrix(dal$data))
dal <- normalize_data(dal, norm_method = "cycloess")
write_qc_report(dal,
  color_column = "group", output_dir = reports,
  filename = "qc_post.pdf", overwrite = TRUE
)
invisible(dev.off())
stopifnot(identical(dal$metadata$sample_id, colnames(dal$data)))
```

The same three proteins in the same four runs, before and after. Missing cells stay missing.

```{r}
#| label: before-after
round(before[1:3, 1:4], 2)
round(as.matrix(dal$data)[1:3, 1:4], 2)
```

Each run's intensity quantiles (5, 25, 50, 75 and 95%) before and after. Normalisation should pull
the run medians together.

```{r}
#| label: quantiles
intensity_quantiles <- function(values, stage) {
  probs <- c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95)
  qs <- apply(values, 2, quantile, probs = probs, na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(
    stage = stage, sample_id = colnames(values),
    q05 = qs[1, ], q25 = qs[2, ], q50 = qs[3, ], q75 = qs[4, ], q95 = qs[5, ]
  )
}
stopifnot(identical(colnames(before), colnames(dal$data)))
quantiles <- bind_rows(
  intensity_quantiles(before, "before"), intensity_quantiles(as.matrix(dal$data), "after")
) |>
  left_join(select(dal$metadata, sample_id, arm, timepoint), by = "sample_id")
quantiles |>
  group_by(stage) |>
  summarise(median_of_run_medians = median(q50), spread_of_run_medians = diff(range(q50)))
```

## How much of each protein's variance the design explains

Eta squared is the share of a protein's variance that the six group-by-time cells (HR or LR at T1,
T2, T3) explain: 0 means the cells explain nothing, 1 means they explain everything. It is computed
from a limma fit of `~ group` per protein, needs at least 4 observed runs, and is descriptive.
Nothing downstream reads it.

```{r}
#| label: eta-squared
cell_fit <- lmFit(dal$data, model.matrix(~group, dal$metadata))
total_ss <- apply(dal$data, 1, \(x) sum((x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))^2, na.rm = TRUE))
eta2 <- 1 - cell_fit$sigma^2 * cell_fit$df.residual / total_ss
eta2[rowSums(!is.na(dal$data)) < 4] <- NA
summary(eta2)
```

## Runs after normalisation

Principal component analysis (PCA) needs a complete matrix, so each run's gaps are filled with that
run's median, for this picture only. The saved matrix keeps them missing.

```{r}
#| label: pca
filled <- apply(dal$data, 2, \(x) replace(x, is.na(x), median(x, na.rm = TRUE)))
pca <- prcomp(t(filled), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
components <- tibble(
  component = paste0("PC", 1:4),
  variance_explained = round(summary(pca)$importance[2, 1:4], 3)
)
pca_scores <- as_tibble(pca$x[, 1:2], rownames = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(dal$metadata, by = "sample_id")
components
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pca
#| fig-cap: "Runs on the first two principal components after normalisation, gaps median-filled."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.5
ggplot(pca_scores, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = timepoint, shape = arm)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(T1 = "#E69F00", T2 = "#0072B2", T3 = "#009E73")) +
  labs(
    x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", 100 * components$variance_explained[1]),
    y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", 100 * components$variance_explained[2])
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

## Summary

`r nrow(dal$data)` proteins in `r ncol(dal$data)` runs were normalised. The six group-by-time cells
explain a median `r round(100 * median(eta2, na.rm = TRUE))`% of a protein's variance. PC1 and PC2
carry `r 100 * components$variance_explained[1]`% and `r 100 * components$variance_explained[2]`%
of the variance.

## Save

`DAList_normalized.rds` is the input to `03_Quantification` and `04_Gene_Sets`; the workbook is read
by `Figures/S01_QC`.

```{r}
#| label: save
saveRDS(dal, file.path(out, "DAList_normalized.rds"), compress = "xz")
sheets <- list(
  normalized = bind_cols(
    as_tibble(dal$annotation) |> select(uniprot_id, protein, gene, description),
    as_tibble(dal$data)
  ),
  components = components,
  pca_scores = select(pca_scores, sample_id, subject, arm, timepoint, PC1, PC2),
  eta_squared = tibble(uniprot_id = rownames(dal$data), eta2 = unname(eta2)),
  intensity_quantiles = quantiles
)
holds <- c(
  "Cyclic-loess log2 abundance, one row per protein.",
  "Variance explained by the first four principal components.",
  "Each sample's PC1 and PC2 score.",
  "Share of each protein's variance explained by the six group cells.",
  "Each sample's log2 intensity quantiles (5, 25, 50, 75, 95%) before and after cyclic loess."
)
write_workbook(sheets, holds, file.path(out, "normalisation.xlsx"), inputs, paths)
```
